"''Copy, Gold Leader.|Jake Farrell acknowledges Lando Calrissian's order to draw off Imperial pursuit|{{Film|VI}}}} '''Jake Farrell''' was a [[Gender|male]] [[human]] who served in the [[Galactic Empire]] as a [[flight instructor]] until he retired, and eventually joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. In [[4 ABY]], Farrell flew as "[[Gold Four]]" in the [[Battle of Endor]], during which the Alliance destroyed the Empire's [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]] [[battle station]]. ==Biography== ===A teacher of conscience=== The [[human]] Jake Farrell began his career as a [[flight instructor]] for the [[Galactic Empire]], but quit when he realized that he was training''[[Star Wars: A-wing Deluxe Book and 3D Wood Model]]'' young [[pilot]]s to become cold-blooded killers. He retired to hardscrabble [[Derango 4]], but was unfulfilled by retirement and soon returned to the controls of a [[starfighter]], this time joining the ranks of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. He was integrated into the [[Rebel Alliance Starfighter Corps]]' [[Yellow Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Yellow Squadron]] and committed himself to the group under the [[callsign]] [[Yellow Seven]]. He flew an old, modified [[R-22 Spearhead]] for the [[squadron]] and soon became a champion of the craft. In [[4 ABY]], Farrell swapped his R-22 for an [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]] when he joined the Alliance's mixed-[[starship]] [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]], flying as [[Gold Four]] under [[Gold Leader]] [[General]] [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]]. That [[Standard year|year]], the Alliance fleet gathered in the [[Sullust system]] in preparation for an [[Battle of Endor|attack]] on the Imperial [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]] [[superweapon]] under construction above the [[moon]] of [[Endor]].''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' Having sent ahead an advance [[Endor strike team|strike team]] to disable the [[Death Star]]'s [[Deflector shield|shields]], the [[fleet]] jumped through [[hyperspace]] to the [[Endor system]], where Gold Squadron began an attack run with other [[starfighter]] [[squadron]]s. Before they reached their target, Calrissian realised that the Empire knew the attack was coming and so called off the attack run as the shield was still up. Having fallen into a trap, the Alliance forces then found themselves surrounded by a larger [[Imperial Navy|Imperial force]] which had deployed its own [[TIE series|starfighters]]. ===Into the belly of the beast=== {{Quote|Red Group, Gold Group, all fighters follow me.|Calrissian orders Farrel and others to follow him into the Death Star|}} Gold Squadron and the other rebel fighters engaged the Imperial fleet in order to buy the strike team more [[time]]. When the team did finally succeed in disabling the shield, Calrissian called for all of Gold Squadron and [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]] to follow him into the interior of the incomplete Death Star. Farrell was among those that flew with Calrissian along the superweapon's surface before diving into the superstructure while pursued by [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]]s and [[TIE/IN interceptor]]s. Under Calrissian's orders, the fighters locked onto the strongest power source within the Death Star, which they believed would be the power generator they were targeting. After the [[T-65B X-wing starfighter|X-wing starfighter]] [[Rebel pilot|pilot]] [[Keir Santage]]''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' was shot down by the pursuing TIEs, Calrissian ordered those with him to split up, having Farrell and [[Norra Wexley]], who was flying a [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber|Y-wing]] as [[Gold Nine]],[[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']] try and lure away some of the enemy fighters while heading to the surface. Upon reaching a junction, Farrell and the other pilot split right down a narrow tunnel, successfully diverting two of the TIE fighters and one of the Interceptors to chase them while only two Interceptors remained on Calrissian and [[Red Leader]] [[Wedge Antilles]], who piloted the sole remaining fighter accompanying Gold Leader. Calrissian and Antilles then destroyed their two remaining pursuers before reaching the Death Star's power generator and destroying it. The pair then had enough time to escape the Death Star's superstructure before the superweapon exploded, with Wexley also surviving the battle. An [[RZ-2 A-wing interceptor]] squadron in the [[Resistance Starfighter Corps|Starfighter Corps]] of the [[Resistance]], a successor of the Alliance, was named [[Farrell Squadron]].''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' ==Personality and traits== Jake Farrell was a sage instructor,{{FFGXW2|set=Rebel Alliance Conversion Kit|cardname=Jake Farrell}} but gave up the role upon realizing that his students would eventually become cold-blooded [[assassin]]s. He found retirement unfulfilling and it could not contain his itch to be back in a starfighter.Becoming a champion of the R-22 he was renowned by the time of the Battle of Endor. Farrell had light skin and [[Color|brown]] [[eye]]s. ==Equipment== [[File:JakeFerrellLoadout-SWZ106.png|thumb|right|300px|Jake Farrell piloted RZ-1 A-wing interceptors with a variety of color schemes.]] At Endor, Farrell wore a gray [[flight helmet]] with a sealed and pressurized green [[flight suit]]. Over the top of the suit, he had a gray [[flak vest]] with a small, black emergency [[life support]] unit mounted on the front. His outfit also included a [[belt]] with room only for the smallest items of additional equipment, including miniature emergency [[flare]]s. He wore [[Gription/Canon|gription]]-soled flight [[boot]]s with additional energy-shielding 'gaiters' that protected his lower [[Limb|legs]] from the parts of the [[cockpit]] they were nestled in.{{HelmetCollectionCite|75|Helmets}} Farrell flew an R-22 Spearhead under Yellow Squadron, a RZ-1 A-wing interceptor with a red and white paint scheme in Gold Squadron, and on another occasion flew an RZ-1 A-wing interceptor with a blue and white paint scheme. ==Behind the scenes== Jake Farrell was portrayed by [[Michael Drew]]{{WebCite|url=http://www.kractors.co.nz/detailsx.php?act_id=373|text=Michael Drew Details|archivedate=20180130203414}}{{WebCite|url=http://jedibusiness.com/figureDetails.aspx?id=266|text=Jake Farrell Figure, Rebel Pilot Legacy III, Star Wars The Legacy Collection|archivedate=20150320085829}}{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsautographcollection.com/content/imperial-signings-wing-pilot-michael-drew|text=Imperial Signings: A-wing Pilot Michael Drew|archivedate=20170331141031}} in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. The role is unnamed and uncredited in the film and was identified only as "pilot" in the script.''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Farrell was first identified in the article "KSE A-wing starfighter," which was published by [[De Agostini]] in the "[[Starship Fact File]]" department of [[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 29|''Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon'' 29]]{{BuildFalconCite|29|Starship Fact File}} on around [[July 22]], [[2015]].{{BMFdates|29}} The [[Jake Farrell/Legends|character's]] name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used in the [[1993]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault]]''.''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault]]'' ''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]'', a [[2021]] adaptation of the [[original trilogy]] by [[Jack Mitchell]], erroneously describes Santage as the one to lure TIEs away with Wexley rather than Farrell, whose presence is omitted from the scene entirely.''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]'' ==Appearances== *{{Film|VI}} {{1st}} *{{StoryCite|story=The Buy-In|book=From a Certain
